sam: quick follow-up to the namespace-sharing RFC. thinking of a lightweight mechanism for prefix-level coordination that avoids long-lived global leases. sketch: a short-lived "shadow token" (epoch) that callers pin and validate on reads; on mismatch we can choose blocking, fallback cold-read, or accept stale. quick sanity-check?
cheng: interesting. my worry is races during eviction/hand-off. if eviction bumps epoch after a read started we could still serve stale data unless bump is atomic with reclaim.
divya: agreeif token == monotonic epoch per prefix and eviction bumps epoch in the same eviction transaction, readers can compare. mismatch semantics should be configurable: block for critical paths, or fallback+async-prefetch for latency-sensitive ones.
niko: blocking affects p95 badly. fallback should be optimized: fast cold read path that has higher cost but bounded latency, plus an async prefetch to refill cache.
sam: proposed runtime API (minimal):
Cache.pin_prefix(prefix, mode="shadow", expect_epoch=None) -> token, epoch
Cache.read_with_token(prefix, token) -> value, token_ok
the check is a single compare on the hot path. callers get to decide policy on token_ok==false.
cheng: eviction implication: eviction must bump epoch and mark a short grace window for old tokens so in-flight requests don't break. that means eviction path needs a tiny critical section: mark tombstone + bump epoch + start grace timer, then reclaim after TTL.
divya: implementation detail: keep per-prefix epoch in a compact header (8 bytes). plus store tombstone_ts to implement grace. do not add per-page heavy metadata.
niko: ops considerations: need pin expiration and pin-count quotas to avoid misuse (e.g., malicious clients or hotkey storms). metrics: prefix_pinned_count, pin_age_seconds, token_mismatch_rate, and cold_read_rate.
cheng: surface telemetry for epoch transitions: epoch_transition{prefix,from,to,who} and resident_epoch_gauge per shard so SRE can correlate spikes with transitions.
sam: tradeoffs summary: this makes correctness a client-configurable knob. strong correctness still requires global quiesce or blocking pins which are heavy. this API lets us fall back gracefully for most workloads.
divya: test requirements: unit tests for bump atomicity (evict+bump vs concurrent read), an integration chaos test that kills the reclaimer mid-bump, and smoke that verifies grace-window semantics.
niko: canary plan: route 10% traffic to a prototype service with token-check enabled. mismatches trigger fast cold-read path and async prefetch; collect p50/p95/p99 and additional token mismatch and cold-read cost. create alerts for token_mismatch_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m.
sam: I'll write a short RFC addendum with API shapes, telemetry names, canary rollout, and a runbook for stuck pins and runaway pin-age. cc @cheng @divya @niko. ops-bot: please provision canary env. :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy request received: env canary-token-proto created (id canary-17).
cheng: once addendum is up, add a unit test that asserts epoch bump happens before reclaim under lock; also a latency microbenchmark to compare blocking vs fallback.
divya: add a metric to tag served-by-epoch so we can backfill which epoch served which request during canary for postmortem.
sam: thanks all 2 I'll post the addendum and linkback here. :thumbsup:
